pages.title: A fraction is just division
pages.text:
a/b means a ÷ b. The top is how many pieces you have, the bottom is what size they are.

Three moves cover almost everything:
• MULTIPLY: top × top, bottom × bottom. Easy.
• DIVIDE: flip the second one, then multiply.
• ADD / SUBTRACT: only once the bottoms match.

steps.why: You can only add pieces that are the same size.
Multiply top and bottom by 3. Same value, new size.
Add the tops, keep the bottom.

pages.title: Canceling: only what's multiplied
pages.text:
(3x)/(6x) → cancel x, then 3/6 = 1/2. Fine, because x is MULTIPLIED on both top and bottom.

(x + 2)/x → you CANNOT cancel the x. It's added on top, not multiplied.

Same idea: (x + 3)/x = x/x + 3/x = 1 + 3/x (splitting the TOP is fine), but 1/(x + 3) can't be split.

pages.title: What an exponent means
pages.text:
x³ = x·x·x. Every rule comes from that.

• x³·x² = (x·x·x)(x·x) = x⁵ → multiply: ADD powers
• x⁵/x² = x³ → divide: SUBTRACT powers
• (x²)³ = x²·x²·x² = x⁶ → power of a power: MULTIPLY
• x⁰ = 1
• x⁻ⁿ = 1/xⁿ → negative = flip to the bottom
• (2x)³ = 8x³ → the power hits everything in the brackets

pages.title: Why calculus cares
pages.text:
The power rule (xⁿ → n·xⁿ⁻¹) only works on xⁿ. So before differentiating, rewrite everything as x to a power:

1/x² → x⁻²
√x → x^(1/2)
3/√x → 3x^(−1/2)

Rewriting is half the problem on most quiz questions.

steps.why: x³ on the bottom flips up with a minus.
Going down from −3 means MORE negative.
Flip back for a clean answer.

pages.why: Same base, multiplying → add the powers: 2 + 5 = 7.

pages.title: The one idea
pages.text:
√x = x^(1/2)
∛x = x^(1/3)
√(x³) = x^(3/2)

The exponent is a fraction: TOP = the power, BOTTOM = which root.

Once a root is an exponent, all the exponent rules work on it.

steps.why: Rewrite the root as a power.
Power rule: bring ½ down, subtract 1.
Fraction subtraction: give 1 the same bottom.

pages.title: What roots don't do
pages.text:
√(ab) = √a·√b ✓
√(a/b) = √a/√b ✓
√(a + b) = √a + √b ✗  (√(9+16) = 5, not 7)

Same pattern as fractions and logs: sums don't split.

pages.q: 1/√x as a power of x is…
pages.why: Root → ½. On the bottom → negative. Together: x^(−½).

pages.title: What a log asks
pages.text:
log₂ 8 asks: 2 to the WHAT gives 8? Answer: 3, because 2³ = 8.

ln x is the same thing with base e (≈ 2.718): ln x asks 'e to the what gives x?'

So:
• ln 1 = 0 (e⁰ = 1)
• ln e = 1 (e¹ = e)
• ln and e undo each other: ln(eˣ) = x, e^(ln x) = x

pages.title: The three log rules
pages.text:
• ln(ab) = ln a + ln b → times becomes plus
• ln(a/b) = ln a − ln b → divide becomes minus
• ln(aⁿ) = n ln a → a power comes out front

And the trap: ln(a + b) has NO rule. Leave it alone.

pages.why: A power INSIDE the log comes out front as a multiplier.

choices: No rule: leave it as ln(a + b)
pages.why: ln a + ln b is ln(ab), the product. Sums inside a log don't split.
